did_you_know.text: Did you know? Psalm 76 opens with a musical heading: “For the director, with stringed instruments,” and is identified as a psalm and a song of Asaph.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes that the Lord is especially known in Judah, and that his name is great in Israel.
Did you know? According to the psalm, the Lord’s dwelling place is described as being in Salem and in Zion—names associated with Jerusalem.
Did you know? In Zion, the Lord is described as breaking the weapons of war: the flashing arrows, shield, sword, and weapons of battle.
Did you know? The psalm describes the Lord as glorious and resplendent, comparing his power to mountains rich in prey.
Did you know? The enemy’s mighty warriors are described as losing their strength and falling into sleep; even the men of valor are unable to use their hands.
Did you know? The rebuke of the God of Jacob brings sleep not only to the warriors but also to the chariot and the horse—a symbol of military power rendered unable to act.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes awe of the Lord and asks, “Who can stand before you” when you reveal your anger?
Did you know? When the Lord pronounces judgment from heaven, the earth is described as fearing and becoming still.
Did you know? The purpose of the Lord’s rising to judge is presented as the salvation of all the humble of the earth.
